note.explanation: Most everyday materials are mixtures: they contain more than one element or compound mixed together. A mixture can have a uniform composition, like salt water, or a non-uniform composition, like rock.
examples: Salt water is a homogeneous mixture because its concentration is uniform throughout.
Rock is a heterogeneous mixture because its constituents are not distributed uniformly.
note.simple: An element has one kind of atom. A compound has different elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. A mixture has substances mixed together in any ratio.
note.checkQuestion: Which form of matter is made when more than one type of element or compound is mixed together in any ratio?
note.title: Elements, compounds and mixtures
steps: Check whether the sample contains one kind of atom, different elements chemically combined, or substances mixed together.
If substances are mixed, check whether the composition is uniform throughout or varies from place to place.
Name it as an element, compound, homogeneous mixture or heterogeneous mixture.
note.answer: A mixture is formed when more than one type of element or compound is mixed together in any ratio.

options: A pure substance containing only one kind of atom
Two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
Two or more substances mixed in any ratio
A sample with a composition that varies from place to place
mcqs.stem: Which description best identifies an element?
rationales: Correct: the textbook defines an element as a pure substance containing the same kind of atoms.
Incorrect: this describes a compound, not an element.
Incorrect: this describes a mixture.
Incorrect: a composition that varies across a sample is a feature of a heterogeneous mixture.

rationales: Incorrect: copper is an element.

options: A fixed ratio
Any ratio
A ratio that changes from one part to another
No elements or compounds
mcqs.stem: In what ratio may the substances in a mixture be combined?
rationales: Incorrect: a fixed ratio is characteristic of a compound.
Correct: a mixture forms when substances are combined in any ratio.
Incorrect: variation from place to place may describe a heterogeneous mixture, but it does not define the ratio in which its substances are mixed.
Incorrect: mixtures are made from elements or compounds, or both.

rationales: Correct: salt water is homogeneous because its concentration is uniform throughout.
Incorrect: air is given as an everyday mixture, but not as the textbook's example of a homogeneous mixture here.

options: Its composition is uniform throughout
It contains only one kind of atom

mcqs.stem: Which feature identifies a heterogeneous mixture?
rationales: Incorrect: uniform composition throughout describes a homogeneous mixture.
Incorrect: one kind of atom describes an element.
Incorrect: chemically joined constituents in a fixed ratio describe a compound.
Correct: a heterogeneous mixture has different concentrations of its constituents in different parts.

options: A pure substance with the same kind of atoms
A pure substance made of different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
Elements or compounds mixed in any ratio

mcqs.stem: Which description best identifies a compound?
rationales: Incorrect: this is the definition of an element.
Correct: a compound is made of different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
Incorrect: this describes a mixture.
Incorrect: compounds have uniform composition, not necessarily non-uniform composition.

options: It has the same concentration throughout
Its components are different in different parts
It contains only one type of element
Its components are chemically bonded in a fixed ratio
mcqs.stem: What makes a salt-water solution homogeneous?
rationales: Correct: the textbook says its concentration is uniform throughout.
Incorrect: different composition in different parts describes a heterogeneous mixture.
Incorrect: salt water contains more than one substance.
Incorrect: fixed-ratio chemical bonding describes a compound, not a solution.

explain.title: Element
explain.body: Element is the simplest form of matter. It is a pure substance containing the same kind of atoms. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by ordinary chemical reactions.

explain.title: Compound
explain.body: Compound is also a pure substance. It is made up of two or more different chemically elements combined in a fixed ratio. When elements come together, they react with each other and form chemical bonds that are not easy to break.

explain.title: Mixture
explain.body: A mixture is formed when more than one types of elements or compounds are mixed together in any ratio. Air, soil, milk and tap water are everyday examples of mixtures.

explain.title: Two kinds of mixtures
explain.body: A mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous. A solution of salt and water is an example of homogeneous mixture because its concentration is uniform throughout. A sample of rock is an example of heterogeneous mixture because the concentration of its constituents is different in its different parts.

explain.title: Check the composition
explain.body: The composition and properties of an element or a compound are uniform throughout a given sample and from one sample to another. To identify a mixture, look for substances mixed together; then check whether their composition is uniform throughout.

mistakes: Calling a compound a mixture: a compound's elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
Calling every mixture heterogeneous: salt water is homogeneous because its concentration is uniform throughout.
Confusing an element with a compound: an element contains the same kind of atoms, while a compound contains different elements chemically combined.
Giving an example without the identifying feature: explain uniform composition for a homogeneous mixture or differing composition in different parts for a heterogeneous mixture.
